rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic root sense of intoxication is blocking a path.
rows.anchor: وأصل السكر في اللغة : سد الطريق

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that an Anṣārī gave wine to him and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān before prohibition; while leading Maghrib, Ali recited al-Kāfirūn incorrectly, prompting the verse. Al-Buṣīrī grades the transmitters trustworthy.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه ( أن رجلا من الأنصار دعاه وعبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله تعالى عنه فسقاهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other transmitters clarify the mistaken recitation as “I worship what you worship”; al-Tirmidhī’s version says, “and we worship what you worship.”
rows.anchor: وقد رواه أصحاب السنن الثلاثة وأحمد وعبد بن حميد والبزار والحاكم والطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition lasts until intoxication passes and people understand their words, preventing them from altering what they say in prayer.
rows.anchor: فلا يقع منكم حينئذ تبديل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī takes prayer to mean both the prayer itself and its place, the mosque: the verse bars an intoxicated person from praying and a sexually impure person from being in the mosque.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المراد بالصلاة نفسها وموضعها وهو المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Junub refers to emission of semen, actual or near at hand through the meeting of the circumcised parts; it applies whether semen results from intercourse or otherwise.
rows.anchor: بالتقاء الختانين , لأن الجنابة المني سواء كان عن جماع أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A junub may pass through the mosque without stopping or praying.
rows.anchor: أي مارين مرورا من غير مكث ولا صلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction on junub remains until the body has been deliberately washed.
rows.anchor: أي تغسلوا البدن عمدا

words: وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse orders concessions from the cases most in need of them toward those less in need, beginning with illness and travel.
rows.anchor: مرتبا لها على الأحوج إلى الرخصة فالأحوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travel concession applies to short trips as well as long ones.
rows.anchor: سواء كان السفر طويلا أو قصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ literally means a low, broad place used for relieving oneself; here it means returning from relieving oneself after a necessary bodily function.
rows.anchor: من التخلي فقضى حاجته التي لا بد له منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can cover either skin touching skin or intercourse, whether or not ejaculation occurs; this is placed later because it is less avoidable and less frequent than relieving oneself.
rows.anchor: وأخر هذا لأنه مما منه بد , ولا يتكرر تكرر قضاء الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not finding water includes either its absence or inability to use it.
rows.anchor: أي إما بفقده أو بالعجز عن استعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum means sincerely intending the act and entering into it with that intention; ṣaʿīd is soil and ṭayyib is pure and wholesome.
rows.anchor: اقصدوا قصدا صادقا بأن تلابسوا ناوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description ṭayyib is illustrated by the verse saying that good land brings forth its plants by its Lord’s permission.
rows.anchor: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum is a distinctive act of worship granted to this community.
rows.anchor: وهذه عبادة خاصة بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “your faces” limits the wiping action because dust cannot reach every part; wiping is valid even if it does not cover the hairline.
rows.anchor: ولما كان التراب لا يتمكن من جميع العضو وإن اجتهد الإنسان في ذلك أدخل الباء قاصرا للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands are wiped from the earth, as Sūrat al-Māʾida makes explicit; the wording can indicate that a stone suffices.
rows.anchor: لا فيه ولا عليه مثلا , ليفهم التمعك

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī allows lamastum to mean literal skin contact, intercourse caused by contact, or a particular kind of touching; intercourse can be named by its cause or the whole by a part.
rows.anchor: جوز الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أيضا أن يراد بها المس - أي ملاقاة البشرتين -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition also bars conduct approaching the sin of an intoxicated tongue uttering words unworthy of God.
rows.anchor: نهى عما يدني من وقوع صورة الذنب الذي هو جري اللسان بما لا يليق به سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum alleviates the otherwise severe restriction when using water is difficult or impossible.
rows.anchor: وخفف ما كان شديدا بالتيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw means that God leaves punishment for the offense, especially the error made while intoxicated.
rows.anchor: بترك العقاب على الذنب , وكأن هذا راجع إلى ما وقع حالة السكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafūr adds erasure of the sin; the author connects this to the tayammum concession, which makes prayer virtuous instead of leaving it or praying without purification.
rows.anchor: أي بترك العقاب وبمحو الذنب حتى لا ذكر بعد ذلك أصلا , وكأن ها راجع إلى التيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concession is explained by God’s stated wish not to impose hardship on believers.
rows.anchor: وذلك معنى قوله سبحانه وتعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people rebuked are the People of the Book, who claimed to be the most rightly guided while falsely purifying themselves.
rows.anchor: المرادين بهذه الآيات من أهل الكتاب أضل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their false claims include that the Fire will touch them only a few days, that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise, that they deserve praise for deeds not done, and that believers should follow their desires.
rows.anchor: من قولهم ^ ( { لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة } ) ^

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God purifies, by His complete knowledge, power, wisdom, and justice, praising a person and creating good qualities that produce righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: بما له من العلم التام والقدرة الشاملة والحكمة البالغة والعدل السوي بالثناء عليه وبخلق معاني الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person whom God has purified in a capacity such as prophethood may declare that status to convey what benefits people from God.
rows.anchor: فإذا زكى أحدا من أصفيائه بشيء كالنبوة , كان له أن يزكي نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatīl is the tiny twisted thread in a date stone’s cleft; it stands for neither slight nor great injustice.
rows.anchor: في شق النواة من ذلك الشيء المفتول , أي قليلا ولا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wrongs no one because He knows what each deserves, is the just judge, and has no need to oppress.
rows.anchor: لأنه عالم بما يستحقون وهو الحكم العدل الغني عن الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inimitability of God’s speech in both elaboration and concision proves the People of the Book’s falsehood, sharpening the rebuke that follows.
rows.anchor: الإعجاز في حالتي الإطناب والإيجاز ؛ ثبت كذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabrication is deliberate and brazen: they lie about the God who knows everything and can punish them.
rows.anchor: أي يتعمدون { على الله } أي الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using “to” rather than “them” intensifies censure, stresses their distance from noble presences, and suggests knowing defiance; their scripture is truly from God.
rows.anchor: ولكنه قال - لزيادة التقريع والتوبيخ والإعلام بأن كفرهم عناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jibt can mean an idol, soothsayer, magician, anything without good, or anything worshipped besides God; all senses fit here and are forbidden in their scripture.
rows.anchor: وهو الصنم والكاهن والساحر والذي لا خير فيه وكل ما عبد من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghut can mean al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, a soothsayer, Satan, a leader of misguidance, idols, or anything worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وهو اللات والعزى والكاهن والشيطان وكل رأس ضلال والأصنام وكل ما عبد من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root basis of taghut is exceeding bounds through aggression; the word is singular but can also be used collectively.
rows.anchor: وأصله ومداره مجاوزة الحد عدوانا , وهو واحد وقد يكون جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers conceal what their intellects disclosed through God’s signs.
rows.anchor: أي ستروا ما أظهرته عقولهم بسببها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise to put them in the Fire is certain even if they receive a long reprieve.
rows.anchor: بوعد ثابت وإن طال معه الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When skins reach the state of cooked meat, like dead flesh in a wound, they no longer feel pain.
rows.anchor: الذي أدرك أن يؤكل , فصارت كاللحم الميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restores skins to their pre-burning state; like reshaping a silver ring, the material remains while its form changes, so the new skin differs in form.
rows.anchor: قبل تسليط النار عليها , كما إذا صغت من خاتم خاتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Renewed skins renew the tasting of torment and the spectacle of restoration, matching their repeated denials; otherwise their worn bodies would perish and their punishment end.
rows.anchor: فتجدد لهم مشاهدة الإعادة بعد البلى كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is unconquerable and perfects His acts; He apportions punishment to sins because the condemned intended to persist in them for as long as they lived.
rows.anchor: يتقن صنعه , فجعل عذابهم على قدر ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Profession of faith followed by righteous deeds demonstrates that believers are sincere in their faith.
rows.anchor: أقروا بالإيمان { وعملوا } بيانا لصدقهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shorter promise-form sa-nudkhiluhum, compared with sawfa for the disbelievers, may suggest believers wait less, have shorter lives, or enter Paradise before other saved groups.
rows.anchor: وربما أفهم التنفيس لهم بالسين دون سوف - كما في الكافرين - أنهم أقصر الأمم مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens’ ground is so well watered that every place in them is suitable for a river to flow.
rows.anchor: أي إن أرضها في غاية الري , كل موضع منها صالح لأن تجري منه نهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise specifies their lasting residence in the gardens forever.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر قيامها وما به دوامها , أتبعه ما تهواه النفوس من استمرار الإقامة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the beauty of the abode, the passage turns to the beauty of its companions.
rows.anchor: ولما وصف حسن الدار ذكر حسن الجار فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After food comes drink; the verse identifies prohibited drinks and implies that other drinks remain permitted, paralleling the surah’s earlier prohibition following permission for cattle.
rows.anchor: ولما تم بيان حال المأكل وكان داعية إلى المشرب , احتيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reminds believers that faith means submission and obedience.
rows.anchor: مذكرا لهم بما أقروا به من الإيمان الذي معناه الإذعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr means every intoxicant, with no distinction between a small amount and a large amount.
rows.anchor: وهي كل ما أسكر سواء فيه قليله وكثيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other practices share religious and worldly harms, cause quarrels and loud oath-taking, and are all pagan customs; listing them reinforces that drinkers, idol sacrificers, and lot-users are alike.
rows.anchor: ما واخاها في الضرر دينا ودنيا وفي كونه سببا للخصام وكثرة اللغط المقتضي للحلف والإقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to the earlier discussion of gambling in Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تقدم ذكره في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idol-stones and divining arrows were mentioned earlier at the beginning of this surah.
rows.anchor: المتقدم أيضا ذكرهما أول السورة

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī says a zalam is an arrow without feathers.
rows.anchor: الزلم : القدح لا ريش له - قاله البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their order pairs wine’s waste of wealth with gambling, gambling’s financial corruption with idols’ religious corruption, then manifest shirk in idol worship with the hidden shirk of divining arrows.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الخمر غاية في الحمل على إتلاف المال , قرن بها ما يليها في ذلك وهو القمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs is filth deserving avoidance in every respect, whether physical or abstract and whether the impurity is sensory or conceptual.
rows.anchor: أي قذر أهل لأن يبعد عنه بكل اعتبار حتى عن ذكره سواء كان عينا أو معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular predicate explicitly attaches to wine; predicates for the other three items are elided and understood separately, since one collective predicate does not suffice.
rows.anchor: ووحد الخبر للنص على الخمر والإعلام بأن أخبار الثلاثة حذفت وقدرت , لأنها أهل لأن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the practices Satan’s work heightens repulsion by associating them with the accursed, remote one.
rows.anchor: أي المحترق البعيد , ثم صرح بما اقتضاه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtināb means deliberately keeping oneself on a side apart from the prohibited thing; the singular form follows from the preceding unified ruling.
rows.anchor: أي تعمدوا أن تكونوا عنه في جانب آخر غير جانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success means attaining all one’s aims, which cannot be achieved while engaging in these practices.
rows.anchor: أي تظفرون بجميع مطالبكم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that when wine was prohibited, there was none in Medina; another version says five kinds of drink were present, but none was grape wine.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال : ( لقد حرمت الخمر وما بالمدينة منها شيء )

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: From the Prophet’s pulpit, ʿUmar reports that wine prohibition covered drinks made from grapes, raisins, dates, honey, wheat, and barley, and defines wine as what veils the intellect.
rows.anchor: سمعت عمر على منبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : أما بعد

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that while he served date wine to Abū Ṭalḥa and others, a messenger announced prohibition; they immediately ordered the jars poured out and neither questioned nor revisited the matter.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : ( ما كان لنا خمر غير فضيخكم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: In another report, Anas says grape wine was scarce in Medina at prohibition and most wine was made from fresh or dried dates.
rows.anchor: وي رواية عنه : ( حرمت علينا الخمر حين حرمت وما نجد خمر الأعناب إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī dates the prohibition to a few days after the Battle of the Trench.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : وذلك بعد غزوة الأحزاب بأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains the reason for banning wine and gambling because these are its primary targets; the bans on idols and arrows had already been explained as fisq, and believers already avoided them.
rows.anchor: اقتصر على بيان علة النهي عن الخمر والميسر إعلاما بأنهما المقصودان بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s aim is to provoke enmity and hatred by enticing people to drink and gamble.
rows.anchor: أي بتزيين الشرب والقمار لكم { أن يوقع بينكم العداوة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine removes restraint, exposes hidden grudges, criticism, and envy, and can lead to long wars and grave calamities.
rows.anchor: لأن الخمر تزيل العقل , فيزول المانع من إظهار الكامن من الضغائن والمناقشة والمحاسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gambling consumes wealth and breeds resentment toward the person who takes it, disrupting the loser’s circumstances.
rows.anchor: والميسر يذهب المال فيوجب ذلك الإحنة على من سلبه ماله ونغص عليه أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine plainly distracts from remembrance and prayer; gambling distracts the winner through elation and the loser through consuming distress.
rows.anchor: أما في الخمر فواضح , وأما في الميسر فلأن الفائز ينسى ببطر الغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic, fixed-form question presses the hearers to stop, after the exclusive attribution to Satan, pagan associations, stated ruling, and warnings of harm.
rows.anchor: وأعظم التهديد بالاستفهام والجملة الاسمية الدالة على الثبات بعد التأكيد بالحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb “obey” intensifies the command to follow God and the Messenger in avoiding the prohibited practices.
rows.anchor: وأكد الأمر بإعادة العامل فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to beware warns against disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي من المخالفة , ثم بلغ الغاية في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means engaging in any of the prohibited conduct; the verb’s form suggests struggling against one’s original disposition to do so.
rows.anchor: أي بالإقبال على شيء من ذلك , وأشار بصيغة التفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who turn away harm only themselves, since the proof has been established and the Messenger’s sole duty is clear conveyance.
rows.anchor: أنكم لم تضروا إلا أنفسكم , لأن الحجة قد قامت عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger’s clear conveyance echoes the command to deliver what was sent down from the Lord.
rows.anchor: وهذا ناظر إلى قوله : ^ ( { بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك } ) ^

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever chooses disbelief for himself should consider the coming punishment; God does not guide one who chooses disbelief.
rows.anchor: فمن اختار لنفسه المخالفة كفر , و الله لا يهدي من كان مختارا لنفسه الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every report has a place and time when its truth or falsehood will settle; no report escapes that outcome.
rows.anchor: موضع ووقت قرار من صدق أو كذب , أي لا بد أن يحط الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will learn the outcome is certain even if its realization is delayed.
rows.anchor: بوعد صادق لا خلف فيه وإن تأخر وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is addressed while the warning is intended for others, making the rebuke more deterrent.
rows.anchor: خاطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد غيره ليكون أردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To indulge in the signs is to speak without reflection or insight, following desire like someone wading blindly into water and unable to see where error lies.
rows.anchor: بل طوع الهوى , كما يفعل خائض الماء في وضعه لرجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means leaving their gathering or doing whatever amounts to ending the association.
rows.anchor: بترك المجالسة أو ما يقوم مقامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even their discussion of other matters is treated as rambling, since it contains both trivial and weighty talk without the ordering discipline of religious law.
rows.anchor: أيضا بالخوض , لأن فيه الغث والسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording of Satan’s causing forgetfulness stresses that this instruction is important enough not to forget.
rows.anchor: أي إنساء عظيما إشارة إلى أن مثل هذا الأمر جدير بأن لا ينسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the reminder, the text names them as wrongdoers rather than using a pronoun, generalizing the warning and identifying darkness as the cause of their conduct.
rows.anchor: على الوصف الذي هو سبب الخوض , وهو الكون في الظلام

words: وَمَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Meccan instruction addresses a time when believers could not object openly; if the unbelievers were stronger, the pious bore no sin for remaining among them.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الآية مكية , وكانوا إذ ذاك عاجزين عن الإنكار بغير القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on sitting with mockers is not because the weak believers incur guilt by association; separation instead makes their disapproval visible.
rows.anchor: وما نهينا عن المجالسة لأن عليهم فيها - والحالة هذه - إثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the gathering reminds the mockers, who may be embarrassed at harming a companion and thereby avoid the irreverence.
rows.anchor: إظهارا للكراهة { ذكرى } للخائضين لاستحيائهم من أذى الجليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope is that the mockers will become people expected to fear God and will avoid derision out of respect for their companion.
rows.anchor: حال من يرجى منه التقوى , فيجتنب الخوض في الآيات إكراما للجليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited promise that God’s blessings cannot be counted frames the signs of creation discussed here.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها } ) 77 [ إبراهيم : 34 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Splitting seeds and date stones to bring forth plants is a kind of enlivening and displays God’s repeated care.
rows.anchor: ولما كان فلقهما عن النبات من جنس الإحياء لما فيه من النمو فسر معنى الفلق وبينه إشارة إلى الاعتناء به وقتا بعد وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living growth includes plants, trees, birds, and animals emerging from seeds, date stones, eggs, and semen; this is an argument against denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي كالنجم والشجر والطير والدواب { من الميت } من الحب والنوى والبيض والنطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle signals a stable, undisputed fact, unlike the preceding verb that expresses renewed action.
rows.anchor: معبرا باسم الفاعل الدال على الثبات لأنه لا منازعة لهم فيه , فلم تدع حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also brings dead matter, such as seeds, out of living plants and other living things, further clarifying His power to produce opposites.
rows.anchor: أي من الحب وما معه { من الحي } أي من النجم وما معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing forth opposites prevents attributing their production to nature or inherent properties, which might seem plausible if each thing produced only its own kind.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم - لو كان لا يخرج عن شيء إلا مثله - أن الفاعل الطبيعة والخاصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can perform these acts; no alleged partner can match Him in any shared divine action, so only He deserves divinity.
rows.anchor: ولا مكافئ له سبحانه وتعالى في شيء من الأشياء فلا شريك له بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks how, and from what direction, people are turned away from the belief they ought to hold.
rows.anchor: أي فكيف ومن أي وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from the lower, familiar world to the celestial realm; its signs of renewed life also answer Abraham’s argument against deifying light, darkness, and stars.
rows.anchor: شارحا لما أشار إليه الخليل عليه السلام في محاجة قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means bringing dawn into being by splitting night’s darkness; common usage attributes the split to dawn without ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وحقيقته : فالق ظلمة الليل عن الصباح , لكنه لما كثر استعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq can also mean disclosure: the cause, splitting, expresses its result, bringing what was hidden into view.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد بالفلق الكشف , لأنه يكشف من المفلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form al-iṣbāḥ evokes entering the morning, allowing the phrase to mean splitting stillness with light or with the movement that follows dawn.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الصباح بهذه الصيغة التي يقال المدخول في الصبح لتصلح لإرادة فلق السكون بالنور أو غيره عن التصرف بالحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the dark night a repose in which and toward which people settle and rest.
rows.anchor: بما يكون من إظلامه { سكنا } يسكن الناس فيه وإليه ويستريحون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the verse as an example of ihtibāk, a paired ellipsis structure.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك
